$schema_note: Sidecar to fields.json. NOT generated by build_spec.py - hand-maintained. The loader merges these keys over fields.json at load time, so a regenerate of fields.json leaves this file untouched. See spec/README.md. WHAT BELONGS HERE, since B2 moved two things out of it into the register: keys that name a FUNCTION in the frontend (child_spec, lookup_filter_expr, default_by), and the prototype's recorded DEPARTURES from the register (type_override, label_override, note, unexpressed) - a departure is a finding for the reviewer, not a correction to apply. What does NOT belong here is anything an admin should be able to set: that is a register column, edited in Administration and published. computed_expr and stage_scoped were both on the wrong side of that line until migration 0015.

conventions.identifiers: Bare api_name of a field in the SAME module. Leading digits (3rd_party_one_time) and em-dashes (guarantee_—_value) are legal.
conventions.picklist_comparison: In computed_expr and visibility_condition, a string literal compared against a picklist or multiselect field is normalised through spec/picklists.json - it matches on either the key or the label. So `deal_source == 'Partner-sourced'` holds whether the stored value is PARTNER_SOURCED or 'Partner-sourced'.
conventions.lookup_filter_comparison: lookup_filter_expr runs against records in the TARGET collection, which are seed rows, not spec fields - no picklist is available to normalise through. String comparison there is slug-normalised instead (case-folded, and -/_/space treated as equivalent), because the seed is inconsistent: accounts.account_types holds labels ('End Client') while users.roles holds keys ('BD_OWNER').
conventions.percent_unit: UNRESOLVED IN THE SPEC. seed/regions.json stores region_pricing_pct as 1 meaning 100%, i.e. a fraction. Nothing states the convention for Discount % or Probability %. net_line_total below assumes discount is a fraction. Flagged on the Spec Health page.
conventions.child_spec_columns: A child_spec column is either an INLINE object (api_name, label, type, required, width, plus picklist / lookup_target / lookup_filter_expr / computed_expr as the type needs) or a '<module>.<api_name>' REF to a field the register already carries. A ref means 'this column IS that field' and inherits its type, picklist, lookup, formula and requirement - which is how the milestone_—_* and guarantee_—_* fields become row columns without being restated, and why Planned Date is required while the other three milestone dates are not. Both forms are resolved to the same shape at load, and a cell renders through the same FieldControl every other field on the screen uses.
conventions.child_row_expressions: A computed_expr on a child column is evaluated ONCE PER ROW. Its identifiers resolve to a sibling column of the row FIRST and to a field of the parent record second, so 'guarantee_—_value / contract_value' reads the row's guarantee value and the deal's contract value in one expression. A name in neither namespace throws rather than evaluating to null. lookup_filter_expr on a child column keeps its normal semantics - it runs against the TARGET collection only, so it cannot see the parent record; a filter like 'contacts at this lead's End Client' is not expressible and is recorded in open_questions.

list_views.$note: Which columns a module's list screen shows, in order. Every entry is a '<module>.<api_name>' ref into fields.json, so a list can never name a column the register does not carry. The register has no list-view sheet at all - this is the fourth thing the workbook should grow a column for.

partners.$note: A VIEW OVER accounts, not a collection of its own. The columns are accounts.* refs because a partner IS an account whose account_type includes a partner type - there is no second organisation record. See partner_roster below for which types qualify.

registrations.$note: The registrations collection is described by the partners MODULE, section DEAL REGISTRATION - see MODULE_OF_COLLECTION in src/lib/spec/index.ts. The partner column is FULLY QUALIFIED because partners.partner is defined twice - here and in QUARTERLY SCORECARD - and the loader refuses to resolve the short form.

leads.$note: days_since_last_update is Computed with no computed_expr in the register (see seed_normalisation.leads below and Spec Health) - the list cell derives it from modified_date/created_date directly rather than through the formula engine. lead_id is DELIBERATELY NOT A COLUMN: a record id is addressing, not information, and the row already navigates to the record by its name. The id is still on the record page as its subtitle, and leadListCell still knows how to render lead_id if the column is ever put back - it is an autonumber the store never stores under that key, so the cell reads the record id instead.

opportunities.$note: opportunity_name and end_client are read_through fields (see spec/module_split.json) - an Opportunity record does not store them, so the LIST endpoint's raw-row search and sort cannot reach them (see mocks/query.ts, which reads row[api_name] directly and never walks a parent chain). The record page resolves them correctly via useResolvedRecord; this list's cells do the same, per row - see opportunityListCell.tsx. search is left empty so the query layer falls back to every STORED field of the module rather than searching a field that would silently match nothing. Recorded as an open question rather than patched here: the fix belongs in the list endpoint, not in a sidecar.

deals.$note: deal_id is DELIBERATELY NOT A COLUMN, same as leads.lead_id above - the id is addressing rather than information, and the row navigates by name. dealListCell still renders it if the column is put back.

partner_roster.$note: Which accounts.account_type values put an organisation on the Partners list. The register never says. leads.customer_partner_si filters on PARTNER_SI alone, but seed/accounts.json gives Schneider Electric (OEM_TECHNOLOGY_PARTNER) a partner_tier and a partner_type, so the register plainly considers an OEM a partner too. Recorded as an open question rather than guessed at silently.

partner_registration.$note: Numbers the Partner Playbook §6.2 states and the register does not carry as data. exclusivity_days duplicates what partners.exclusivity_expiry_date's computed_expr already encodes; it is repeated here because the chip and the acknowledgement modal need the number before any record exists.
partner_registration.$exclusivity_days_note: 89, NOT 90. The window includes the start day, so a registration acknowledged on 13 Jan runs to 12 Apr. The journey document is authoritative on this. The register's own prose still reads 'Start date plus 90 days' on partners.exclusivity_expiry_date and is wrong by one day - flagged in open_questions and shown in the field's tooltip so a reviewer sees both.
partner_registration.$acknowledgement_sla_note: §6.2 states 48 HOURS. partners.submitted_date and acknowledged_date are both typed `date`, so the rule can only be applied to whole days and is expressed as 2 days everywhere on screen. Nothing displays or computes hours - see precision_limits.

capture_fields.$note: The seven fields a partner supplies when registering. Everything else in DEAL REGISTRATION is stamped by ARK on acknowledgement, so a create form that offered them would invite somebody to type an exclusivity date by hand.

adjudication_criteria.$note: The three criteria §6.2 says an adjudication is recorded against. These ARE in the register - partners.who_registered_first, stronger_client_relationship, better_delivery_capability, orders 19-21 - so they are rendered from it rather than invented here. This block only records that these three, and no others, are the criteria.

adjudication_outcome.$note: The rest of a CONFLICT ADJUDICATION record - what the BD Director decides once the three criteria above are assessed. Split from the criteria only so the screen can label them separately; both sets render from the register. conflict_id is excluded because it is an autonumber ARK assigns, and registration_a / registration_b because the pair is determined by the collision that raised the adjudication, not typed by hand - the screen stamps them.

quick_create.$note: CreateNewDialog's '+ Create new' shortcut on a lookup field shows only the target module's first section - enough to make the record selectable, not a full create form. A few fields outside that first section matter from day one, though, and skipping them just because they sit in a later section would be a real gap. Listed here, by module, as extra api_names appended after the first section's own fields; each still goes through the normal visibility/requirement rules.
quick_create.$contacts_note: leads.primary_contact's '+ Create new' was showing only CORE (name, title, account, email...) with no way to say WHO this person is to the deal - Contact Role sits alone at the top of ROLE & RELATIONSHIP and is exactly that.

seed_normalisation.$note: spec/seed/*.json is generated from the workbook's seed sheets, and its keys do not match the api_names build_spec.py emits into fields.json from the register sheets. The two sheets were filled in by different people. Renaming the seed by hand would be undone by the next regenerate, so the mapping lives here and is applied once when the store loads. EVERY ENTRY BELOW IS A DEFECT IN THE WORKBOOK, not a design choice - see spec/README.md and the Spec Health page.

registrations.$note: No renames needed - every key in seed/registrations.json is a real partners api_name. The entry exists for the picklist coercion: the seed writes partner_role "Prime" and registration_status "Active", both labels, where the register's keys are PRIME and ACTIVE.

leads.$note: seed/leads.json was filled in against an earlier draft of the register: it spells the suite fields 'saap' where the register settled on 'sap', and writes 'probability' where the register calls the field probability_pct. project_stage is seeded as a bare integer (3) rather than the picklist key (3_PRESCRIPTION) - the generic picklist coercion below now stringifies a numeric value first, so it resolves through the same key-prefix match already used for contact_role codes.

opportunities.$note: Derived Opportunity rows cross the pipeline split after Lead seed normalization. This entry ensures picklist values in an already-persisted Opportunity are coerced on migration too.

precision_limits.$note: Places where the register's chosen TYPE cannot carry the rule the playbook states. These are not gaps to fill and not defects to correct - the type is a reasonable choice and changing it would cost more than the precision is worth. They are listed so nobody later reads a screen as claiming more accuracy than the data has.

rows.detail: §6.2 gives acknowledgement a 48-HOUR SLA. submitted_date and acknowledged_date are both `date`, so elapsed time is only knowable to the whole day. The prototype states the rule as 2 days and reads results as 'acknowledged in 1 day, inside the 2-day rule'. It never displays or computes hours. A registration submitted at 23:00 and acknowledged 26 hours later counts as 1 day; one submitted at 01:00 and acknowledged 46 hours later counts as 2. Both are inside the rule, and neither is distinguishable from the data. Making this exact would mean typing both fields datetime, which is a real change to the register - raise it only if 48 hours is meant literally rather than as 'within two working days'.

The 2-day rule counts CALENDAR days, not business days. bids_pocs.sla_met uses business_days() for its own SLA, so the register is inconsistent about which it means. A registration submitted on a Friday is late by Sunday. Left as calendar days because §6.2 says 48 hours, which is a wall-clock measure.

open_questions.$note: Gaps found by hand while building a screen, which no automatic check over fields.json can detect. They render on the Spec Health page beside the generated ones. `ref` is a module.api_name where one applies and a module name where the question is about the sheet as a whole.

rows.detail: The Partners sheet defines no partner-ORGANISATION fields. Its three sections are DEAL REGISTRATION, CONFLICT ADJUDICATION and QUARTERLY SCORECARD - all child records of a partner. The partner-only attributes (Partner Tier, Partner Type, Platform Depth, Partner Satisfaction Score, Engagement Cadence, Post-Award Protection, Protected Until) are a section of the ACCOUNTS sheet. The prototype therefore keeps them on the account and does NOT create a second partner record keyed by account_id, which would store the same seven values in two places. Decide: move them to a PARTNER PROFILE section on the Partners sheet, or confirm they belong on Accounts.

No lookup_filter, so any account at all can be named as the partner on a deal registration - including one whose account_type is End Client only. leads.customer_partner_si does carry a filter (Account Type must include Partner / SI). Should the registration lookup match it, and should it also admit OEM / Technology Partner? Left unfiltered rather than guessed at.
No lookup_filter, where leads.end_client has one. Same question as partners.partner. Left unfiltered.

THE REGISTER IS WRONG BY ONE DAY. Its prose reads 'Start date plus 90 days', which would make a registration acknowledged on 13 Jan expire on the 13th of April. The journey document says 12 Apr, because the 90 days INCLUDE the start day. The sidecar therefore computes add_days(start, 89) and the seed rows agree; the register's prose still says 90 and is shown in the field's tooltip beside a note saying so. Restate it as 'start date plus 89 days' or as '90 days inclusive of the start date' - the ambiguity is the actual defect, and it will recur wherever else the register counts a window.

The picklist carries Submitted, Acknowledged, Active, Extended, Expired, Superseded and Rejected, but nothing states which transitions ARK performs and which a person sets. In particular NO RULE EXPIRES A REGISTRATION - a row can sit at Active forever with a date months behind it. The chip is derived from the dates and shows the stored status alongside it when the two disagree, rather than believing either. The seed no longer trips this, since it is rebased to demo day, so a warning appearing on screen now means a real contradiction rather than stale seed data.

requirement = Conditional with no condition, and nothing anywhere says how long an extension runs or who may grant one. No extend action is offered, because the length of the window it would create is not stated.

Nothing says which account types make an organisation a partner. seed/accounts.json gives Schneider Electric (OEM / Technology Partner) both a partner_tier and a partner_type, so the roster cannot be Partner / SI alone. The prototype lists Partner / SI and OEM / Technology Partner - see partner_roster in spec/extensions.json. Consultant / Specifier and Sector Specialist are excluded, on no better evidence than that the seed gives them no partner attributes.

PROTOTYPE SEED EDIT, not a register question. e& Enterprise (ACC-002) has had End Client added alongside Partner / SI in spec/seed/accounts.json, so the journey's own partner demonstrates the dual-type model. The workbook's seed sheet still gives it Partner / SI alone, and build_spec.py will overwrite this on the next regenerate - make the same change there. Core42 (ACC-004) already carried both.

seed/leads.json writes project_stage as a bare integer (3) and deal_source as a label ("Partner-sourced"), where the register types both as picklists whose keys are 3_PRESCRIPTION and PARTNER_SOURCED. Create Lead From Registration writes the register's keys, because that is what the form engine reads - so a lead created that way does not match the seed rows beside it. The leads collection has no seed_normalisation entry yet; adding one belongs with the Leads module. Note that resolvePicklistValue only coerces strings, so the integer stages pass through silently and are not currently reported.

CONFLICT ADJUDICATION describes a record with no seed data and no stated trigger beyond 'created when two partners register the same client and project'. The registration screen detects that collision and warns, but does not create a conflict record: nothing says whether ARK raises one automatically or a person does.

PROTOTYPE SEED EDIT. The suite lookup now offers exactly seven: S!aP Omnific, S!aP Cognus, S!aP Kolaz, S!aP KIM, S!aP Mazzant, S!aP Agentic AI, IVAR (Gorilla). The five that existed kept their SKUs (SEG-OMN, SEG-COG, SEG-KLZ, SEG-KIM, SEG-MAZ) and were only RENAMED to carry the S!aP prefix - seed/leads.json and all 35 price-matrix rows reference them by SKU, so renaming the name is safe and renaming the SKU would not be. SEG-AGAI and SEG-IVAR are new rows. build_spec.py will overwrite all of this on the next regenerate; make the same edit in the workbook's product sheet.

THE REGISTER HAS NO 'SUITE TYPE'. leads.sap_solution_suite's lookup_filter reads 'Suite Type must be Primary suite', but a catalogue item carries no such attribute - the closest thing is catalogue_category, whose values are Module, Segment Library, User Pack, Add-On, Service, Support. The filter is therefore bound to catalogue_category = Segment Library. That works only while 'the suites' and 'the Segment Library category' are the same set, which they now are by construction. Either restate the register's filter as 'Catalogue Category must be Segment Library', or add a real Suite Type field and say which items are Primary suites.

TWO PROBLEMS WITH THE TWO SUITES ADDED AT REVIEW. (1) 'S!aP Agentic AI' (SEG-AGAI, Segment Library) sits alongside the pre-existing 'S!aP Agentic (S!a)' (SAP-AGNT, Module). Either they are the same capability sold two ways and the catalogue should say so, or they are different things whose names are too close to tell apart on a quote. (2) 'IVAR (Gorilla)' is the only suite not S!aP-branded, and it is carried under Segment Library because that is where the suite lookup reads from - confirm that is where it belongs rather than being its own product line. NEITHER NEW SUITE HAS PRICE-MATRIX ROWS: seed/prices.json covers the five original SKUs across seven sizes and nothing was invented for these two, so they cannot be quoted until the price book supplies them.

NOT FILTERED, where sap_solution_suite now is. Suite Demonstrated at Stage 1 is a product lookup with no lookup_filter in the register, so it still offers the whole catalogue - modules, add-ons and user packs included. That may be deliberate, since a demo can cover a module rather than a whole suite. Decide whether it should be restricted to the same seven, and note leads.secondary_sap_suites has the same question: it is a multiselect with no picklist behind it at all.

NOTHING SAYS WHAT AN ADJUDICATION DOES TO THE LOSING REGISTRATION. The decision picklist awards the deal to Registration A, Registration B or neither, but no rule anywhere changes the other registration's registration_status, releases its exclusivity window, or stops it being used to create a lead. The screen therefore records the decision and then OFFERS 'Mark REG-000nn Superseded' as a separate, explicit action rather than applying it as a side effect - superseding is what SUPERSEDED plainly means and what Convert to Deal already does on award, but here it is an inference and is left to a person. State the rule: does an adjudication supersede the loser automatically, and does it also end that partner's exclusivity early?

PROTOTYPE ID CONVENTION, not from the register. Conflict records are created as CONF-0001 (four digits, following GATE-0091). CLAUDE.md's Conventions list ids for leads, deals, quotes, registrations and gates but not for a conflict. Confirm or replace the prefix.

THE REGISTER DOES NOT SAY WHICH SIDE OF A COLLISION IS A AND WHICH IS B, and the decision picklist is written entirely in those terms (Awarded to Registration A). The screen stamps the registration being viewed as A and the colliding one as B, which means the same conflict reached from the other registration's screen would name the slots the other way round if a second record were created. The prototype prevents that by matching an existing adjudication in EITHER direction, so one pair only ever has one record - but the register should still state the rule, for instance that A is always the earlier submitted_date.
expiring_within_days = 15, the threshold behind the amber Expiring chip, is not in the register. It was chosen for the prototype. Confirm or replace it.

PROTOTYPE SEED EDIT. spec/seed/registrations.json has been rewritten so both rows use expiry = start + 89 and so the pair sits inside one 89-day window of the anchor date - REG-00051 now runs 24 Oct 2025 to 21 Jan 2026 rather than 3 Jun to 1 Sep 2026. Without it the two registrations are 141 days apart and no single anchor can show one Active and one Expiring at the same time. The workbook's seed sheet needs the same correction.

THE REGISTER DEFINES NO ROW SHAPE FOR ANY CHILD LIST IN LEADS OR DEALS - all six. It plainly knows how: the bids_pocs sheet carries BID CHECKLIST ITEM (child), TBE QUERY (child), POC SUCCESS CRITERION (child) and POC USE CASE (children) as explicit child sections with their own typed columns. Nothing equivalent was written for demo_attendees, feature_gaps_logged, payment_milestones, bid_commitments_register, expansion_use_cases or linked_expansion_leads. Every child_spec in this file is therefore origin: 'inferred' and each one names its basis; the screens render working tables so BD can correct the columns in front of the data, but the register still says nothing. The fix is child sections on the leads and deals sheets, in the bids_pocs style.

PROTOTYPE REGISTER EDIT, made by hand in spec/fields.json and spec/picklists.json at review. STAGE 1 - DEMO PRESENTATION was changed in seven ways and build_spec.py WILL OVERWRITE ALL OF IT on the next regenerate - make the same changes in the workbook. (1) product_team_briefed_date REMOVED. (2) demo_debrief_completed_date REMOVED. (3) competitors_mentioned retyped from multiselect to text, max_length 255 - it was a multiselect with no picklist behind it, so it was already free entry and the type was simply wrong. (4) demo_debrief_notes ADDED as longtext directly above demo_completed. (5) leads__agreed_next_step GAINED the value 'Implementation' (key IMPLEMENTATION, sort 4); 'None' moved to sort 5 so it stays last. (6) THREE fields ADDED beneath agreed_next_step, all conditional on it being 'POC scoping': data_site_access_confirmation_document (file), pilot_commercial_model (picklist), pilot_fee (currency). (7) A NEW PICKLIST leads__pilot_commercial_model = Free / Paid. The section is now 27-39 and every later leads row shifted by +3, so the module stays contiguous. See the entries below for what this did to E1.3 and X1.2.

PROTOTYPE REGISTER EDIT. Three fields REMOVED by hand from spec/fields.json at review - parent_account (CORE), post_award_protection and protected_until (PARTNER ATTRIBUTES). build_spec.py will restore all three on the next regenerate; delete them in the workbook too. Removing parent_account also removes the only way the register expressed an account hierarchy, which matters for the two-party model: a client group with several operating companies now has no way to say so.

PROTOTYPE REGISTER EDIT. Field REMOVED by hand from spec/fields.json at review, along with its child_spec above - nothing in the prototype ever populated it (Stage 9 does not create leads) and it was not used by the Deals backend build. build_spec.py will restore it on the next regenerate; delete it in the workbook too if it is to stay gone. Exit criterion X9.1 in spec/criteria.json still reads `linked_expansion_leads.count >= 1` as its source - with the field gone, src/lib/readiness.ts's evaluateCriterionLike fails to resolve the identifier and the check falls open to a manual 'warn' rather than a hard failure, the same fail-open posture the rest of the spec engine takes on a broken expression. Left as-is rather than rewritten, since a replacement source was not specified.

REMOVING THIS BROKE A PARTNER PLAYBOOK RULE - DECIDE WHAT REPLACES IT. Convert to Deal used to write post_award_protection = true and protected_until = booking + 365 days onto the Customer (Partner / SI) account, and the conversion dialog told the user so. With both fields gone there is nowhere to store it, so the step now writes an AUTOMATION LOG entry instead of a record (CLAUDE.md rule 6) and the dialog says as much rather than claiming an effect it no longer has. The rule itself still has no duration stated in the register - 365 days was always a prototype default, unlike the 89-day registration exclusivity window. Either restore the two fields, or state that post-award protection is not tracked.

PROTOTYPE REGISTER EDIT. Four fields REMOVED by hand from spec/fields.json at review - reports_to (CORE), score_captured_date, score_updated_date and blocker_strategy (ROLE & RELATIONSHIP). Make the same deletions in the workbook. Two consequences worth stating: reports_to was the only expression of a client org chart, which is what a stakeholder map needs; and relationship_score now has no captured or updated date beside it, so nothing records WHEN a score was taken or how stale it is.

NEW FIELD, added at review beside BD Owner in STAGE 0 - CONNECT (order 6). Two things to confirm. (1) It is OPTIONAL. Stage 0 is called Connect and entry criterion E1.1 reads 'Contact confirmed and meeting scheduled', which argues for Mandatory - but making a NEW field mandatory retro-blocks every lead already in the pipeline, so it was left optional deliberately. (2) It is UNFILTERED. It should plainly offer only contacts at the End Client or the Customer / Partner, but lookup_filter_expr is evaluated against the target collection alone and cannot see the parent record - the same limitation recorded against leads.demo_attendees. Also decide whether 'Primary Contact' is the right name, or whether this is the same thing the stakeholder map wants.

PROTOTYPE REGISTER EDIT. Was competitive_threats, a multiselect with no picklist behind it in STAGE 4 - RFP / RFI. Retyped to text (max_length 255) and renamed to Competitors Noticed. THE API_NAME WAS RENAMED TOO, from competitive_threats to competitors_noticed, because the two names mean different things and leaving the old one would mislead anyone writing an expression against it later. Nothing referenced it, so nothing broke. Note the register now carries two similar free-text fields - competitors_mentioned at Stage 1 and competitors_noticed at Stage 4; confirm they are meant to be separate captures rather than one field written twice.

THE FOUR milestone_—_* FIELDS NO LONGER RENDER AS LOOSE FIELDS. The register writes them flat in STAGE 7 - CLOSE, but they describe one ROW of Payment Milestones, not one value on the lead - which is why the child_spec references them as columns. Showing them both ways gave two places to type the same thing, only one of which is kept. They are NOT deleted: a field that some child_spec names as a ref column is now treated as belonging to the row, so it renders only as a column and is excluded from record-level validation. That second half matters - milestone_—_planned_date is Mandatory from Stage 7, so hiding the loose field without excluding it would have blocked 7 -> Deal forever with no box to fill. THE SAME RULE APPLIES TO THE SEVEN deals.guarantee_—_* FIELDS, which had the identical problem in ON CONVERSION; say so if Deals should keep showing them loose. The real fix is for the register to write these as child sections, the way the bids_pocs sheet already does.

PILOT FEE IS NESTED ONE LEVEL DEEPER THAN ASKED FOR - CONFIRM. All three new fields were requested as 'conditional on Agreed Next Step = POC scoping'. Pilot Fee is instead visible when agreed_next_step == 'POC scoping' AND pilot_commercial_model == 'Paid', because a free pilot has no fee and demanding one would be a business rule nobody stated. If the register means the fee box to show for a free pilot too - to record a waived or notional value, say - drop the second clause from both visibility_condition and condition.

THE THREE NEW POC FIELDS CARRY A `condition`, WHICH MAKES THEM REQUIRED WHEN VISIBLE - CONFIRM. Every other Conditional field in the register has an empty condition and is therefore treated as optional (see the 'Conditional fields with no condition' group on Spec Health). These three break that pattern deliberately: entry criterion E2.1 demands data or site access confirmed IN WRITING before Stage 2 and gate G1 POC Brief checks the same thing, so a POC agreed with no access document and no commercial model is exactly the gap the gate exists to catch. If they are meant to be prompts rather than demands, clear `condition` and leave `visibility_condition` alone. Note this also means they block 1 -> 2 whenever POC scoping is the agreed next step.

'Implementation' was added as an agreed next step, but nothing states what it MEANS for the pipeline. Every other value names a Stage the lead moves toward - POC scoping to Stage 2, Prescription to Stage 3, RFP to Stage 4. Implementation has no stage behind it: Stage 8 PROJECT SUCCESS is a Deal, not a Lead, and a lead cannot reach it without converting at Stage 7. Either Implementation means 'skip straight to Close', or it means this demo was for an existing client and the work is already sold. Say which, because a reviewer choosing it will expect the pipeline to do something.

THE NEW FIELD INHERITED THE STAGE RULES OF THE ONE IT REPLACED - CONFIRM THIS. demo_debrief_completed_date was Mandatory from Stage 1, blocking 1 -> 2, required_on_skip false, and it was the automatic source of blocking exit criterion X1.2 'Product Team debrief completed'. Removing it would have left X1.2 with nothing to check, so Stage 1 would have quietly lost its debrief gate. demo_debrief_notes therefore carries the same four settings and X1.2 now reads it instead. Nobody asked for the new field to be mandatory - if the debrief is meant to be optional, downgrade it here AND decide what X1.2 checks instead.

ENTRY CRITERION E1.3 HAS NO SOURCE ANY MORE. 'Product Team briefed on client context and sector' was evaluated automatically against product_team_briefed_date, which has been removed. The criterion is a playbook rule (§3.2 S1) so it has NOT been deleted - its source is now null and its evaluation is 'manual', which makes the readiness panel show it as a check a person confirms rather than a check that silently fails forever. Either restore a field that evidences the brief, or accept it as a manual attestation.

A lookup INSIDE a child row cannot be filtered by the parent record. lookup_filter_expr is evaluated against rows of the target collection alone, so 'contacts at this lead's End Client or Customer / Partner' has nothing to bind to and the Attendee column lists every contact. Either the expression language grows a way to reach the parent record (a `parent.` prefix), or the register accepts an unfiltered attendee lookup. Same question will hit any child lookup that should narrow by its parent.

The field is described as 'every commitment made during bid and negotiation', its use_case points at TBE responses becoming delivery obligations, and the only per-row columns the ON CONVERSION section carries are the seven guarantee_—_* fields. A bank guarantee is one kind of bid commitment, not all of them, and there is no column anywhere for the commitment text, the TBE query it answered, or who owns delivering it. Either the field is misnamed and is really a guarantee register, or a second row shape is missing.

values_note says '8 standard milestones' and the description says they carry 'percentages and triggers', but nothing states that a record must hold eight rows, that the percentages must sum to 100, or which milestone triggers which invoice. The proposed row shape reuses administration__milestone, whose eight values match the description exactly - confirm that is the intended set, and state the two rules if they are meant to be enforced.

The Deals sheet declares end_client and customer_partner_si as its own Mandatory lookups, so the split leaves them as stored fields on the Deal — Deals takes 18 of the 20 read-through identity fields rather than all 20. That contradicts carry-forward-by-reference: the same two organisations would then be stored on the Lead, the Opportunity and the Deal, three places to drift. Decide: drop both rows from the Deals sheet and read them through parent_opportunity like the other 18, or state why a Deal is meant to be able to name a different End Client from its Opportunity.

stage_scoped.$note: WHICH fields are per-stage, and whether each carries forward or sticks, are REGISTER COLUMNS now - `stage_scoped` on every row of fields.json, set in Administration. This block used to hold the RULE that derived that set from section names and conditions, which is why nobody could make one field sticky without silently catching four others. Absorbed by backend/absorb_sidecar.py against migration 0015; the open_questions entry that asked the workbook for this column is closed and removed. What is left here is what an admin cannot author, because each names a FUNCTION: `carry_forward.fields[].default_by` is a resolver in src/lib/spec/resolvers.ts that seeds an untouched box, and `history_only` names the two reasons the transition dialog writes - those are NOT per-stage at all, the transitions table already carries one per move. `modules` stays because it gates the strip and the Reasons panel as SCREENS, which is a different question from whether a value is kept per stage; modules.is_pipeline would answer it today but changing that is not this pass. Values live at `<api_name>__s<stage>`.

carry_forward.$note: Shown in the metrics strip at the top of every stage, editable there. A stage with no value of its own inherits the nearest EARLIER stage that has one, falling back to the base api_name. Editing the CURRENT stage also writes the base api_name, so list columns, the readiness panel and the probability-band check keep reading one number. THIS LIST NO LONGER DEFINES THE SET - fields.json's `stage_scoped: carry_forward` does, and the strip renders them in register order. It survives only to bind `default_by`, and only progression_pct has one: no formula can guess a close month, and inheriting the earlier stage's answer is the correct seed for the other two.

fields.$note: The forecast date, revised at every stage rather than answered once at Connect - its own use_case says it must be reviewed monthly. Carry-forward and not sticky: a stage that has not revised it INHERITS the last answer, because the previous month's forecast is still the forecast until somebody moves it. That is the opposite of an On Hold Reason, which must never carry. No `default_by`: unlike progression, no formula can guess a close month, and inheriting the earlier stage's answer is the correct seed. Moved out of STAGE 0 - CONNECT and onto all three modules by backend/close_month_record_state.py; the per-stage values it now leaves behind (`expected_close_month__s0` ... `__s9`) are the history Close Date Pushback Count needed and never had.

sticky.$note: The sticky SET is fields.json's `stage_scoped: sticky` now. This block held `sections`, `require_condition` and `extra` - the rule that caught every CROSS-CUTTING row with a visibility_condition. Absorbed by absorb_sidecar.py, which resolved it to six placements: On Hold Reason, Closed Lost Reason Code and Probability Override Justification, on each of the three pipeline modules. Deliberately NOT caught, then or now: Stage Skip Reason and Stage Reversal Reason, both written by the Advance / Change stage dialog as part of the transition, so a second box here would be two places to write one answer - see history_only below; and every computed row (Days in Current Stage, Days Since Last Update), which is record-level state and stays on the Details tab. `extra` named probability_override_justification with `when: probability_out_of_band`, a predicate no expression could express because a stage's band is not a field. That binding was never read: StageScopedFields.tsx names the field directly and calls probabilityBandBreach(). Recorded here rather than left as metadata nothing performs.

history_only.$note: Reason fields the record KEEPS but no form ASKS for. Both are written by the Advance / Change stage dialog as part of recording the transition - and both were ALSO rendering as ordinary editable boxes in CROSS-CUTTING on the Details tab, which is the two-places-to-write-one-answer the sticky note above says must not happen and which nothing was actually enforcing. They are hidden from every form now and read back in the Reasons & Justifications panel, which points at the History tab where the transition that wrote them lives. Record-level rather than per-stage: the transitions table is what carries one reason per move.

$new_fields_retired_note: RETIRED at Round 7. The 27 rows that lived here are now field_definitions rows in PostgreSQL and arrive in spec/fields.json like every other field, so Administration can see and edit them -- previously it could not, because bootstrap_metadata.py deliberately did not import them and they existed in no database table at all. They are still identifiable by origin ('gap-fix -- 14-stage review'), which is what src/lib/spec/index.ts filters on and all that ever distinguished them. The two `structural` flags moved into `fields` above: opportunities.parent_lead, deals.parent_opportunity. `computed_by` on deals.progression_pct was dropped -- D4 settled that the field is a plain editable Number and nothing derives it.
